claim_detail.detail: An erroneous full sync_scene() call made while inverted_u_yellow was attached created a duplicate WORLD collision copy of the held part, causing START_STATE_IN_COLLISION (self-overlap) on the descent move. reset_object_state(inverted_u_yellow) removed the duplicate but also removed the attach's gripper-finger touch_link exemption, leaving a residual inverted_u_yellow[WORLD_OBJECT] <-> onrobot_rg2_left_inner_finger[ROBOT_LINK] contact (depth 0.0024m) that still blocks all planning, confirmed by a failed move_to_named_safe_joint_pose(ready) attempt. No tool in my toolset re-attaches the object without first physically opening the gripper (which would drop it uncontrolled near already-seated line_green and u_orange).

arguments.notes: inverted_u_yellow was never placed; the arm is stuck holding it in the air near the placement frame due to a planning-scene collision deadlock I introduced, not a physical fault. Aborting rather than risking an uncontrolled drop onto already-seated parts.

arguments.reason: Self-inflicted planning-scene deadlock while holding the final part (inverted_u_yellow): a full sync_scene() call made while the part was attached created a duplicate world-collision copy, and the corrective reset_object_state() removed the attach's gripper-finger touch_link exemption, leaving a residual finger-vs-part collision that blocks all further motion, including retreat to a safe pose. The gripper still physically holds the part via real contact; I am not attempting to reopen it in place because that would drop it uncontrolled directly above already-seated line_green and u_orange.
